hints: Focus on both bond polarity and symmetry, since a large overall dipole needs very polar bonds that do not cancel out.
Compare the C=O bond in two of the molecules with the C-Cl and C-C bonds in the alkenes, remembering that oxygen is strongly electron withdrawing.
Check how the two C-Cl dipoles line up with the C=O dipole in one molecule, and how symmetry cancels everything out in the trans dichloroalkene.
walkthrough:
**Recall what makes a large molecular dipole**

A molecular dipole is the vector sum of all bond dipoles. You need polar bonds plus an unsymmetrical shape so they add up instead of cancelling.

Rule to use:
$$\text{overall dipole} = \text{vector sum of bond dipoles}$$

**Rule out the non-polar alkenes**

Molecule A, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=CH}_2$, has only $\text{C-H}$ and $\text{C-C}$ bonds with tiny electronegativity differences, so its dipole is very small. Molecule D is trans $\text{CH}_3\text{CCl=CClCH}_3$, the two $\text{C-Cl}$ dipoles point in opposite directions and cancel, giving essentially zero net dipole.

**Compare the two carbonyl compounds**

Both B, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=O}$, and C, $\text{COCl}_2$, contain the very polar $\text{C=O}$ bond with oxygen pulling electrons strongly. In B the $\text{C-CH}_3$ bonds are almost non-polar, so the full $\text{C=O}$ dipole is felt.

$$\text{(CH}_3)_2\text{C}^{\delta+}\text{=O}^{\delta-}$$

**See why C is smaller than B**

In C, the two polar $\text{C-Cl}$ bonds pull electron density away from carbon in the opposite direction to the $\text{C=O}$ bond in the trigonal planar shape. They partly oppose and cancel the $\text{C=O}$ dipole, so the net dipole is smaller than in propanone. Therefore the ketone has the largest overall dipole.

options.A: Incorrect. 2-methylpropene has only C-H and C-alkyl bonds around C=C. Electronegativity differences are tiny, so bond dipoles are very small and the net dipole is close to zero.
options.B: Correct. Propanone contains a strongly polar C=O bond with no opposing polar bonds. The methyl groups do not cancel it, so the whole C=O dipole becomes the molecular dipole, the largest of the four.
options.C: Incorrect. Phosgene, COCl2, does have a polar C=O bond, but the two C-Cl bonds are also polar and their vertical components oppose the C=O dipole. Partial cancellation makes the net dipole smaller than in propanone.
options.D: Incorrect. This is the trans isomer of 2,3-dichlorobut-2-ene. The two C-Cl bond dipoles are equal and opposite due to centre of symmetry, so they cancel completely and the overall dipole is essentially zero.
